result.title: Inside-JEPA: From Prediction to Relational Grounding in Latent World Models
result.summary: Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) learn world models in latent space, enabling efficient planning but leaving their states opaque. We introduce Inside-JEPA, which places relational channels for ordered entity pairs inside the JEPA latent state and shows that an inverse-dynamics loss can ground these channels without relation labels when its head reads them, either alone or as part of the full state. On Something-Something V2, latent prediction alone performs no better than a random relation head, while inverse-dynamics supervision that recovers actions from channel changes improves relational AUROC by .065-.103 across ten settings with annotated boxes, by .081 on RH20T robot episodes with held-out tasks, and by .050-.061 across five relations using off-the-shelf detection and tracking. An inverse head on entity latents decodes actions more accurately but barely improves relational grounding; shuffled labels, two label-free objectives, and action labels on only 5% of the pairs also fail to ground the channels. Given an action, predicted relational changes approach the quality of observed future relations (AUROC .599 vs .621). For one-step relational goals, a supervised readout of the 16 channels ranks the correct action among the top five of 65 in 43% of cases, compared with 24% for prediction-only latents and 17% for a frequency prior.

AI.brief_summary: 在 JEPA 潜状态中加入面向有序实体对的关系通道，并在 Something-Something V2 与 RH20T 上检验纯潜预测与逆动力学监督能否使这些通道获得关系 grounding。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接诊断视觉潜状态是否保留实体关系、何种监督能让关系可读，与 LVR 的表示保留、贡献分配和监督信号选择密切相关；但研究对象是世界模型规划而非 VLM 推理，结论向推理期 latent 的迁移可供核查。
